claims.text: Traditional EAM references cannot adequately represent the configurational variability of ab initio liquids in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
An ML potential trained on ab initio data should replace the EAM reference in thermodynamic-integration calculations.
Neural-network potentials or Gaussian approximation potentials are suitable examples of the proposed ML reference.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys containing five or more principal elements.
The proposed temperature range extends from near the melting point to approximately 20% above it.
Liquid atomic configurations become highly diverse in this near-melting and superheated temperature range.
Local atomic-environment descriptors can capture many-body interactions.
Using such descriptors allows an ML potential to represent the configurational landscape of an ab initio liquid more accurately than an EAM potential.
An ML potential can reproduce and sample a wider variety of high-temperature liquid configurations than the EAM reference.
More accurate reproduction of liquid configurations improves phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target potentials.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch and associated errors.
The ML reference is predicted to reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by 20–30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The ML-reference calculation is predicted to produce free energies closer to direct ab initio results.
The advantage of an ML reference should be greatest in alloys with high compositional complexity under near-superheating conditions.
The advantage of an ML reference may diminish for less chemically complex alloys or at temperatures far from the melting range.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on the quality and transferability of the training data and on the descriptor set.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing EAM-reference and ML-reference thermodynamic integration against an independent direct ab initio free-energy calculation on the same liquid alloy.
Failure to reduce path mismatch by at least 15–20%, or failure to improve agreement with direct ab initio free energies significantly, would falsify the hypothesis.
